h1: The 6 Best Ninja Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Ninja Air Fryers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 6 best Ninja air fryers, from compact 4-quart baskets to 10-quart DualZone models, compared on capacity and cooking modes.
summary: The Ninja DZ201 8 quart DualZone is the best overall, with two baskets, Match Cook and Smart Finish. The DZ401 10 quart suits large families, and the DZ550 adds a built-in cook thermometer. Among single-basket models, the Air Fryer Pro 5 quart fits couples, the 4 quart is the cheapest, and the Crispi Glass is the unusual design with no listed capacity.
intro: Ninja's air fryer names barely differ from one another, so the model numbers hide the one split that matters. A single basket cooks one food at a time, while DualZone gives you two independent baskets that can be synced to finish together. That is the difference between serving chicken and fries hot at the same minute and serving one while the other waits.

Our editors reviewed six Ninja models from their listings, comparing capacity, basket layout, cooking modes and extras such as a thermometer. We ranked them on how well each fits a real household. Models whose listings omit capacity lost points, because a quart figure is the basic way to size an air fryer for the people you feed.

products.name: Ninja DZ201 Foodi 8 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone 2-Basket Air Fryer with 2
products.verdict: Two baskets and Smart Finish for the best all-round value.
products.description:
The DZ201 is an 8 quart, 6-in-1 DualZone air fryer with two baskets. Match Cook copies settings across both, while Smart Finish times two different foods so they finish together. It roasts, broils and dehydrates as well as air frys. The two baskets let a chicken thigh cook at one temperature while fries run at another.

It leads because it fits most families without the counter footprint of the 10 quart models. It gives up two quarts to the DZ401 but takes less space. Against the single-basket units it removes the batch cooking that makes a weeknight dinner slow. It sits in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Buy it for two to four people cooking mains and sides. The caveats are the large countertop footprint and dehydrating, which takes patience.
products.idealFor: Households of two to four cooking mains and sides.
products.skipIf: You cook for one and have little counter room.

products.name: Ninja DZ401 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone XL 2-Basket Air Fryer with
products.verdict: Ten quarts of family-sized space across two baskets.
products.description:
The DZ401 is a 10 quart DualZone XL with two baskets and the same 6-in-1 modes as the DZ201, including Match Cook, Smart Finish, broil and dehydrate. The two large baskets suit a whole chicken, a tray of wings, or enough fries for a crowd. It sells in the $100 to $200 bucket, the same as the DZ201.

It trails the DZ201 only because two extra quarts of volume are not needed by smaller households, and the footprint grows with them. Against the DZ550 it lacks the thermometer.

Buy it if you feed four or more. Skip it if counter space is limited, since a 10 quart appliance is a permanent fixture, not a drawer item. For a couple, it is a lot of machine and a lot of preheating.

products.name: Ninja DZ550 Foodi 10 Quart 6-in-1 DualZone Smart XL Air Fryer with 2
products.verdict: Adds a cook thermometer to the 10 quart DualZone design.
products.description:
The DZ550 is a 10 quart, 6-in-1 DualZone Smart XL with a built-in cook thermometer for judging doneness, plus Match and Finish and dehydrate modes. A probe lets you cook meat to a target temperature instead of a timer, which prevents both dry chicken and undercooked pork.

It ranks third because the thermometer is the only thing that separates it from the DZ401, and many households will not use a probe often. Size and baskets are otherwise identical, at the same $100 to $200 bucket.

Buy it if you roast meat regularly and want temperature control. Skip it if you never cook large cuts. The caveat: the thermometer adds a step to each cook, and you have to remember to insert it. For fries and frozen foods the DZ401 does the same job.
products.idealFor: Cooks who roast meats and want temperature control.
products.skipIf: You never cook large cuts of meat.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: A 5 quart single basket with four cooking modes.
products.description:
The Ninja Air Fryer Pro (AF141) is a 5 quart single-basket unit with four cooking modes, in the $100 to $200 bucket. One basket means one food at a time, and the body is compact enough for a smaller kitchen.

The jump from 4 quarts to 5 is modest, but at this price DualZone models appear in the same bracket, and they cook two things at once. That keeps the Pro fourth. It makes sense when you want a mid-size basket and have no room for the bigger units.

Buy it if you want a simple, single-basket machine for one or two people. Skip it if you want to cook a main and side together. The caveat is value: for similar money, the DZ201 gives you a second basket and more modes.
products.idealFor: Singles and couples wanting a mid-size basket.
products.skipIf: You want to cook two foods at once.

products.name: Ninja Air Fryer
products.description:
This is a 4 quart Ninja air fryer with 4-in-1 cooking: crisp, roast, reheat and one more mode. At $50 to $100, it is the cheapest Ninja in the guide, and the 4 quart basket suits a single portion or small side.

It sits below the Air Fryer Pro because the basket is a quart smaller, though it saves money and counter space. It cannot match any DualZone model for versatility, and anything beyond two portions needs batches.

Buy it if you cook for one or two people and want the lowest price. Skip it if you regularly feed three or more, because you will run the basket twice for every meal. The compact body stores easily in a cupboard, which is a real advantage in a small kitchen.
products.idealFor: One or two people on a budget.
products.skipIf: You regularly feed three or more.

products.name: Ninja Crispi Glass Air Fryer
products.verdict: A 4-in-1 Ninja with a glass design (model FN101GY).
products.description:
The Ninja Crispi Glass Air Fryer (FN101GY) is a 4-in-1 model in the $100 to $200 bucket, built around a glass design rather than the basket and drawer of the other models. The spec data does not list its capacity.

It lands sixth because the missing capacity makes it hard to compare against the 4 and 5 quart baskets, and it costs more than the entry model. The glass design is the draw, since you can see food browning without opening it.

Buy it if you prefer a glass design and Ninja support. Skip it if you want a confirmed capacity. Before ordering, check the quart figure on the product page and decide whether it fits your portions, because the other models state theirs and cost less.
products.idealFor: Buyers who prefer a glass design.

whatMatters.detail: DualZone models have two baskets that cook separately, and Smart Finish times them to finish together. Single baskets cook one food at a time. If you cook a main and a side, DualZone saves real time, because nothing waits. Check the listing for 2-Basket in the title, not just the product name, because Ninja model numbers look alike.

Quarts measure basket volume. A 4 quart basket suits one or two people, while 8 to 10 quarts suits families. Match the number to your usual portions, which you will find in the product title, usually next to the model name. With DualZone models, check whether the quart figure is the total or per basket.

Four-in-one models crisp, roast and reheat, while six-in-one models add broil and dehydrate. More modes only matter if you will use them. Read the mode list in the bullets, and think honestly about whether you would dehydrate fruit or broil a steak. Most daily use comes down to air fry and roast, which every model here handles.

A probe lets you cook meat to a temperature rather than a time, which removes guesswork on thick cuts and reduces overcooking. The DZ550 lists one. Check the listing for cook thermometer wording if doneness matters, since the other Ninjas here do not state a probe. A probe costs extra counter work, so use it for roasts, not wings.

A 10 quart unit is a large appliance that lives on the counter and rarely gets put away. If you have little room, a 4 or 5 quart model is easier to live with. Check the listed dimensions and leave clearance on all sides for hot air. Measure under your cabinets as well, since hot air needs space to escape.

faq.q: Do the DZ401 and DZ550 differ much?
faq.a: Both are 10 quart DualZone models with two baskets. The DZ550 adds a cook thermometer, which is the main difference. Choose the DZ401 unless you roast meat often, since the rest of the hardware is the same.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with Ninja air fryers?
faq.a: Assuming bigger is better. A 10 quart unit takes a lot of counter room for small portions, and a 4 quart Ninja will do fine for a single eater or a couple.

faq.q: Is DualZone worth it over a single basket?
faq.a: Yes if you cook a main and a side together. Smart Finish times both baskets to end at once, so nothing goes cold while the other cooks. A single basket cannot do that, so the Air Fryer Pro and the 4 quart model need batches.

faq.q: How do I set one up?
faq.a: Wash the baskets, place the unit on a heat-safe surface with clearance on all sides, and preheat as the manual directs. Run an empty cycle first to clear any factory smell, and keep the vents unblocked.

faq.q: How do I clean the baskets?
faq.a: Wipe them after use and wash with a non-abrasive sponge while they are still warm, since grease sets as it cools. Check the manual for dishwasher guidance, and avoid steel wool, which can strip the coating from the baskets.

faq.q: Can I cook frozen food straight in?
faq.a: Air fryers are generally used this way, and a 4 quart or larger basket handles it. Follow package directions, and shake or turn the food halfway for even crisping. Do not overfill the basket, or the air cannot circulate.

finalTake: Buy the DZ201 for most households and a main plus side routine. Choose the DZ401 for four or more eaters, the DZ550 if you cook meat to a temperature, and the single-basket 4 or 5 quart units for one or two people on a budget. Treat the Crispi as a design-led option and confirm its capacity.
